page_title: What do VCs really look for when making investments?

summary.title: What do VCs really look for when making investments?
summary.one_liner: Learn the criteria VCs use to pick startups: market size and return potential, founding team quality, traction and unit economics, and how priorities shift by funding stage.
takeaways: VCs look for potential unicorns with large markets, since a few big wins fund the whole portfolio.
Founder quality, team history, and execution track record weigh heavily, often more than the idea itself.
Traction and unit economics (ARR growth, CAC, LTV, retention, gross margin) matter more as a company moves through stages.
Evaluation priorities shift from team and vision at angel/seed to growth efficiency and margins at Series B and later.
Market conditions change emphasis: after cheap money dried up, VCs focused more on revenue, profitability and burn.
summary.summary: This Quora question thread collects several investor answers on what VCs evaluate. Contributors discuss the shift from story-driven investing to numbers-focused scrutiny when funding tightens, and describe criteria such as TAM, the ability to reach $100M+ revenue in 7–10 years, founder background, product differentiation, and traction. One answer from a late-seed investor gives a practical heuristic: whether the next-round investor might pay 5x the current price. The page also covers stage-by-stage expectations from angel through Series B and beyond, and a longer checklist of criteria with practical heuristics such as the 1-in-10 rule. The content is opinion-based and experiential rather than a formal study.
